title: How Continuous Zoom Reading Works (fixture)
source_text:
The dial's leftmost setting shows nothing but the root gist: a single claim standing in for the whole source.

At full expansion this branch reveals the fine print behind section A, including the exact wording the summary compressed.

Section A also has a short aside that never needed a summary of its own, since it was already brief.

A second short aside sits beside the first, covering a related point that the build step chose not to merge.

Section B opens with a leaf that stayed a leaf because summarising it further would have lost the specific numbers.

Underneath section B's second child is a leaf describing the method in plain terms, short enough to read directly.

Deep inside section B is a leaf holding the first of two edge cases the method has to handle.

Right beside it is the second edge case, which behaves differently enough to deserve its own paragraph.

Section B's third child bottoms out in a single leaf that lists the caveats readers usually ask about.

Section B closes with a leaf summarising who reviewed the work and when it was last revised.

Section C begins with a leaf about the historical context that motivated the whole document in the first place.

A second leaf in section C lays out the competing view that the authors ultimately rejected and why.

Section C's third branch splits into a leaf describing the first proposed fix in careful, testable language.

Beside it sits the second proposed fix, framed as an alternative with different tradeoffs worth weighing.

```
def apply_fix(x):
    # atomic code block, never summarised
    return x * 2
```
